title: HUGE ANNOUNCEMENT 🎁 (You're gonna love this)
summary: NH announces his free programs will be archived and revamped on the Boostcamp app, with no sponsorship money taken, and releases a revamped Guts program in two alternating templates (Black Swordsman, compound-heavy; Berserker Armor, calisthenics-heavy). He explains how to use the app and warns against program hopping and swapping exercises weekly.
claims: Information should be free: every program he has made in four years is free, never paywalled
He partnered with Boostcamp to archive his programs safely because video descriptions or the channel can be taken down
He rejected sponsorship money from Boostcamp to stay independent; Ko-fi donations let him refuse all sponsorships
Paying $50 for a non-personalized program is ridiculous; such programs should be free to the community
The new Guts program has two templates, Black Swordsman (heavier on compounds like bench, deadlift, chin-ups) and Berserker Armor (heavier on calisthenics), meant to be alternated week to week
The revamp corrects the volume distribution between body parts because his thinking evolved since the original two-year-old program
Exercises can be swapped for preferred options, but pick one and keep it; don't swap lifts every week
After 6 months to a year you can rotate exercises weekly, but too much rotation can drop a lift's frequency to once a month, which is not enough
Ignore the 12-week label; run a program as long as possible, a year or two, or indefinitely with the mirror week
Newcomers should run one template for at least 6 months to a year before adding the second; alternating is something you earn
Don't program hop; tracking progress in an app builds ownership and consistency
In Boostcamp, 1A/1B notation marks a superset; the number is the superset and the letter the order
He has about 30 free programs and plans to revamp and move all of them, next likely a Baki calisthenics template
